mainTopic: Grounds for divorce: the משנה's three opinions, their sources in the פסוק, and related teachings about how a husband should treat his wife
overview: The amud opens with a one-line הלכה that closes the previous discussion: the woman is permitted to both men. Then a new משנה brings a three-way מחלוקת about the grounds for divorce. בית שמאי allow it only for ערוה, בית הלל allow it even for burning his food, and רבי עקיבא allows it even if he found a prettier woman. In a ברייתא, בית הלל and בית שמאי argue over the two words ״ערות דבר״. בית שמאי use ״דבר״ to require two witnesses, while בית הלל say the joined phrase carries both readings. The גמרא then explains that רבי עקיבא's dispute with בית שמאי depends on ריש לקיש's rule that ״כי״ has several meanings. רבא rules that a divorce given for no reason still stands, and he condemns a man who plans to divorce his wife while she still lives trustingly with him. Finally, רבי מאיר compares types of husbands to people who find a fly in their drink, and his list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Final ruling: she is permitted to both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the previous discussion with a practical הלכה: the woman is permitted to both men discussed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: she is permitted to both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for the discussion that came just before this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והלכתא signals that the debate is over and we now know what to do in practice. 'Both of them' points back to the two men in the earlier case. The ruling is lenient, so she is not forbidden to either one.
steps.whatToRemember: The previous סוגיא ends leniently: the woman is permitted to both men.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
she is permitted to both of them.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the two men from the case discussed just before this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the preceding part of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, the woman is permitted to both men.

steps.title: בית שמאי: divorce only for forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with בית שמאי, who say a man may divorce his wife only if he found דבר ערוה in her. Their source is a פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say a man may not divorce his wife unless he found in her a matter of ערוה, as the פסוק says: 'Because he found in her ערות דבר.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. בית שמאי give the strictest view: divorce is allowed only for a serious sexual matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי focus on the word ערוה in the פסוק. For them, that word limits divorce to cases of forbidden relations, such as adultery or strong suspicion of it. Smaller complaints are not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of forbidden sexual relations
As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Beit Shammai say:
A man may not divorce his wife,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מָצָא בָּהּ דְּבַר עֶרְוָה –
phrases.english: unless he found in her a matter of forbidden relations,
as it is stated:
"Because he has found some unseemly matter in her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce is allowed only if he found דבר ערוה in her.

steps.title: בית הלל: divorce even for burning his food
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree. They say a man may divorce his wife even for a small fault, like burning his dish, and they quote the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: even if she burned his food, as the פסוק says: 'Because he found in her ערות דבר.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give a much more lenient view than בית שמאי. Any fault is enough grounds for divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both houses quote the exact same words, but they read them differently. בית הלל understand the פסוק as allowing divorce for any kind of shortcoming, not only a sexual one. Burning his dish is their example of a small issue.
steps.confusionAlert: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל quote the identical words 'כי מצא בה ערות דבר.' The disagreement is about how to read the פסוק, not about which פסוק to use.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
Even if she burned his dish,
as it is stated:
"Because he has found some unseemly matter in her."
phrases.notes: It's the same פסוק בית שמאי quoted. בית הלל simply read it differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בית שמאי using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce is allowed even for a minor fault, such as burning his food.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: divorce even if he found a prettier woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא goes even further. A man may divorce his wife even if he found another woman more attractive than her, based on the words 'if she finds no favor in his eyes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: even if he found another woman prettier than her, as the פסוק says: 'And it shall be, if she does not find favor in his eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the most lenient opinion of the three. Even without any fault in her, he may divorce her if he prefers someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses a different phrase from the same פסוק. For him, 'not finding favor in his eyes' is reason enough, even if she did nothing wrong. So the three opinions move from strictest to most lenient.
steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of grounds for divorce: בית שמאי require ערוה, בית הלל allow any fault, and רבי עקיבא allows divorce even when she has no fault at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even if he found another woman better looking than her,
as it is stated:
"And it comes to pass, if she finds no favor in his eyes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, even more lenient opinion, using a different phrase from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce is allowed even if he simply found a more attractive woman.

steps.title: בית הלל challenge בית שמאי from the word 'matter'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. בית הלל challenge בית שמאי: the פסוק says ״דבר״, which means any matter, not only immorality.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: But the Torah already says the word 'matter'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where בית הלל attack בית שמאי's position from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי said a man may divorce his wife only for ערוה. בית הלל answer that the פסוק also says ״דבר״, which sounds like any matter at all. So the פסוק itself seems to allow divorce for smaller faults.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)
But isn't it already stated? (a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a baraita:
Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
But isn't the word "matter" already stated!
phrases.notes: He means ״כי מצא בה ערות דבר״ in דברים 24:1, the same פסוק both sides quoted in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's dispute by bringing a ברייתא with the two sides' arguments.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that divorce is allowed only for ערוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק includes the word ״דבר״, which implies any matter, so divorce should not be limited to immorality.

steps.title: בית שמאי answer back from the word 'unseemly'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer back that the פסוק also says ״ערות״, which points to immorality.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: But the Torah already says the word 'unseemly'!
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back with the other word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side holds on to a different word in the phrase ״ערות דבר״. If any small matter were enough, why would the Torah say ״ערות״ at all? Now בית הלל must explain why both words are needed.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
But isn't the word "unseemly" already stated!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״עֶרְוַת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge to בית הלל's argument from the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's reading that ״דבר״ allows divorce for any matter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק also says ״ערות״, which limits the reason to immorality.

steps.title: בית הלל explain why the Torah needed both words
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל explain that each word teaches something. ״דבר״ teaches that she may be divorced even for a non-immoral matter. ״ערות״ teaches that even a woman divorced for immorality may marry another man.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: If the Torah had said only 'unseemly' and not 'matter', I would have said she leaves her husband because of immorality but not because of any other matter. That is why it says 'matter'. And if it had said only 'matter' and not 'unseemly', I would have said that if she is divorced for a matter she may marry another man, but if she is divorced for immorality she may not marry another man. That is why it says 'unseemly'.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's point by showing that the word ״ערות״ is not extra. It teaches its own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without ״דבר״ we would limit divorce to immorality, so ״דבר״ widens the reasons for divorce. Without ״ערות״ we might think a woman divorced for immorality cannot remarry. Because ״ערות״ is written in the same פסוק, she too may marry another man.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (what we would have thought without this word)
That is why the Torah says it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows בית הלל's method: both words in ״ערות דבר״ are needed, and neither one cancels the other.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
If "unseemly" had been stated and "matter" had not been stated,
I would have said: because of immorality she leaves,
because of some other matter she does not leave;
therefore "matter" is stated.
And if "matter" had been stated and "unseemly" had not been stated,
I would have said: if divorced because of a matter, she may marry another man,
phrases.notes: The next פסוק, דברים 24:2, says the divorced woman may go and become another man's wife.

phrases.english: but if because of immorality, she may not marry another man;
therefore "unseemly" is stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: אִם נֶאֱמַר ״עֶרְוַת״ וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר ״דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's counter-challenge by giving a separate job to each word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word in the פסוק teaches a different law, so neither word is extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only ״ערות״, divorce would be limited to immorality. With only ״דבר״, a woman divorced for immorality could not remarry.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״דבר״ allows divorce for any matter, and ״ערות״ teaches that even a woman divorced for immorality may marry another man.

steps.title: What do בית שמאי learn from the word 'matter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to בית שמאי, who limit divorce to immorality, what does the word ״דבר״ teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, what do they do with this word 'matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to בית שמאי and asks how they explain the word ״דבר״. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל showed that both words have a job in their reading. בית שמאי read the פסוק as speaking only about immorality, so ״דבר״ seems to add nothing for them. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches them.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (how do they explain this word)

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי – הַאי ״דָּבָר״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Beit Shammai, what do they do with this word "matter"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי – הַאי ״דָּבָר״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After בית הלל explained both words, the גמרא asks for בית שמאי's explanation of ״דבר״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson בית שמאי learn from the word ״דבר״

steps.title: 'Matter' teaches that two witnesses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. ״דבר״ appears here and also by witnesses, where a matter is established by two witnesses. So here too, the immorality must be established by two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says 'matter' here, and it says 'matter' there: 'By the mouth of two witnesses or by the mouth of three witnesses shall a matter be established.' Just as there it is with two witnesses, so too here it is with two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that בית שמאי use ״דבר״ to link this פסוק to the פסוק about witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the same word ״דבר״ appears in both places, the rule of one is applied to the other. For בית שמאי, ״דבר״ is not another reason for divorce. It tells us how the ערוה must be proven: through two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here... and it says there (the opening of a גזירה שוה)
Just as there... so too here

phrases.english: "Matter" is stated here,
and "matter" is stated there:
"By the mouth of two witnesses

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל פִּי שְׁלֹשָׁה עֵדִים יָקוּם דָּבָר״;
phrases.english: or by the mouth of three witnesses shall a matter be established";
just as there it is through two witnesses,
so too here it is through two witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי learn from ״דבר״, through a גזירה שוה with the פסוק about witnesses, that the ערוה must be established by two witnesses.

steps.title: בית הלל: the פסוק does not say 'immorality in a matter'
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject בית שמאי's reading. If ״דבר״ meant proof through witnesses, the פסוק should have said ״ערוה בדבר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל: Is it written 'immorality in a matter'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's reply to בית שמאי's גזירה שוה. They say the wording of the פסוק does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״דבר״ described how the immorality is proven, the פסוק would read ״ערוה בדבר״, immorality established by a matter of testimony. It actually says ״ערות דבר״, two words side by side. So בית הלל read ״דבר״ as a separate reason for divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...?! (a way of saying the פסוק does not say that)
Immorality in a matter (established through testimony)

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel: Is it written "immorality in a matter"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's use of ״דבר״ from step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: בית שמאי's reading of ״דבר״ as a requirement of two witnesses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק says ״ערות דבר״, not ״ערוה בדבר״, so the wording does not show that ״דבר״ describes the proof.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the פסוק does not say 'either immorality or a matter'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's reading. If ״דבר״ were a separate reason for divorce, the פסוק should have said ״או ערוה או דבר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי: Is it written 'either immorality or a matter'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's reply: the פסוק does not fit בית הלל's reading either. The next step gives בית הלל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל treat ״ערות״ and ״דבר״ as two separate reasons for divorce. בית שמאי answer that, if so, the Torah should have said ״או ערוה או דבר״. Since it joins the words as ״ערות דבר״, the reason for divorce is ערוה alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Either immorality or a matter (two separate options)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read the same two words, ״ערות דבר״. בית הלל: ״דבר״ allows divorce for any matter, and ״ערות״ teaches that even a woman divorced for immorality may remarry. בית שמאי: only ערוה allows divorce, and ״דבר״ teaches that it must be proven by two witnesses. Each side says the פסוק's wording does not fit the other's reading, and the next step gives בית הלל's answer.
steps.confusionAlert: For בית שמאי, ״דבר״ is not a second reason for divorce. It only tells us how the immorality must be proven: through two witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי – מִי כְּתִיב ״אוֹ עֶרְוָה אוֹ דָּבָר״?!
phrases.english: And Beit Shammai: Is it written "either immorality or a matter"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי – מִי כְּתִיב ״אוֹ עֶרְוָה אוֹ דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 10: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's reading the same way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: בית הלל's reading of ״ערות״ and ״דבר״ as two separate grounds
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק does not say ״או ערוה או דבר״, so the words are not two separate options.

steps.title: בית הלל explain why the verse says ״ערות דבר״
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's challenge. The odd phrase ״ערות דבר״ is used on purpose, so that it can mean this and also that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would say: this is exactly why the verse writes ״ערות דבר״. The phrase can be read this way, and it can also be read that way.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their reading against בית שמאי's last attack. That attack said the verse should have written ״או ערוה או דבר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי argued that if ״דבר״ were a separate reason for divorce, the verse would have said ״או ערוה או דבר״. בית הלל reply that the joined phrase ״ערות דבר״ was chosen so that it carries both readings. It can mean ערוה proven through testimony, like ״ערוה בדבר״, which is the two-witness reading. It can also mean either ערוה or any other matter, like ״או ערוה או דבר״.

keyTerms.meaning: for this reason, that is why
it implies, it can be understood as

phrases.english: And בית הלל [would say]:
For this reason ״ערות דבר״ is written,
since it implies this, and it implies that.
phrases.notes: 'This' is ״ערוה בדבר״, a fault proven by witnesses. 'That' is ״או ערוה או דבר״, any fault at all. The same two words hold both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 on behalf of בית הלל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The unusual wording is intentional and carries more than one meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase ״ערות דבר״ should have been split into ״או ערוה או דבר״ if it meant two reasons.
steps.terutzMaskana: The combined phrase ״ערות דבר״ is read both ways: as ערוה established through two witnesses (״ערוה בדבר״), and as either ערוה or any other matter (״או ערוה או דבר״). So divorce is allowed for any shortcoming.

steps.title: What is the basis of רבי עקיבא's opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא from the משנה, who allows divorce even if the husband found another woman. It asks what the dispute is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that רבי עקיבא says a man may divorce his wife even if he found another woman. On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next opinion in the משנה, that of רבי עקיבא. It asks what the source of his disagreement with בית שמאי is. This sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allows divorce for a reason that has nothing to do with any fault in the wife. The גמרא wants to find what in the verse each side reads differently.

keyTerms.meaning: he found another woman (more pleasing to him)
on what point do they disagree?

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says:
Even if he found another woman.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. He may divorce his wife even if he simply found a woman he likes more.

phrases.english: On what point do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the בית שמאי / בית הלל discussion and opens a new topic: רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which point in the verse is the root of the dispute between רבי עקיבא and the others?

steps.title: The dispute depends on ריש לקיש's rule about ״כי״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute rests on ריש לקיש's teaching. The word ״כי״ can have four different meanings.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about ריש לקיש's teaching. ריש לקיש said that the word ״כי״ is used with four meanings: 'if', 'perhaps', 'rather', and 'because'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the key tool behind the dispute: ריש לקיש's rule about the word ״כי״. The next step shows how each side uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כי״ can mean different things in different verses. So the meaning of ״כי״ in the divorce verse is open to debate. Each side will pick a different meaning, and that choice decides their law.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא ריש לקיש (רבי שמעון בן לקיש)
a Hebrew word with several possible meanings
it is used with four meanings

phrases.english: About [the teaching] of ריש לקיש,
as ריש לקיש said:
״כי״ is used with four meanings:
'if', 'perhaps', 'rather', 'because'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on ריש לקיש's rule that ״כי״ has four meanings.

steps.title: בית שמאי read ״כי״ as 'because'; רבי עקיבא reads it as 'or if'
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי read the verse as 'she did not find favor because he found ערות דבר'. רבי עקיבא reads it as 'she did not find favor, or if he found ערות דבר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold: 'And it will be, if she does not find favor in his eyes, because he found ערות דבר in her.' This means she lost favor because he found ערות דבר. רבי עקיבא holds: 'כי he found ערות דבר in her' means 'or else, if he found ערות דבר in her'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies ריש לקיש's rule. It shows that each side reads ״כי״ in the verse differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, ״כי״ means 'because'. Not finding favor is then explained by ערות דבר, so ערות דבר is the only valid reason. For רבי עקיבא, ״כי״ means 'or if'. Then 'not finding favor in his eyes' is a reason all by itself, even if he simply found someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: she finds favor in his eyes

steps.whatToRemember: The whole dispute hangs on one small word. If ״כי״ means 'because', ערות דבר is the only valid reason (בית שמאי). If ״כי״ means 'or if', simply not finding favor is enough (רבי עקיבא).
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides read the same verse. They are not arguing about which verse to use. They argue only about what the single word ״כי״ means in it.

phrases.english: בית שמאי hold:
'And it will be, if she does not find favor in his eyes,'
'כי he found in her ערות דבר':
because he found in her ערות דבר.
And רבי עקיבא holds:
'כי he found in her ערות דבר':

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי, מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר.
phrases.english: or else, [if] he found in her ערות דבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies ריש לקיש's rule from step 14 to the verse and completes the answer to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי read ״כי״ as 'because', so the only reason is ערות דבר. רבי עקיבא reads it as 'or if', so not finding favor is its own valid reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי עקיבא can allow divorce with no fault in the wife at all: he finds it directly in the wording of the verse.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about a divorce when nothing at all was found
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא what the law is if the husband found neither ערוה nor any other matter in his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: if he found in her neither ערוה nor any other matter, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב פפא asks what happens when the husband has no reason at all for the divorce. The next step gives רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everyone named some reason that allows divorce. רב פפא asks about a case with no reason at all. If such a man divorces anyway, is the divorce good or not?

phrases.english: רב פפא said to רבא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָצָא בָּהּ לֹא עֶרְוָה וְלֹא דָּבָר, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: [If] he found in her neither ערוה nor [any other] matter, what is [the law]?
phrases.notes: He means the husband went ahead and divorced her anyway. Does the divorce work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the discussion of the opinions in the משנה is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law of a divorce given when the husband found neither ערוה nor any other matter in his wife?

steps.title: רבא: Only a rapist must take back his divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a man who divorced without reason does not have to remarry her. Only for an אונס did the Torah say he must take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We learn it from what the Torah revealed about an אונס: "He may not send her away all his days." All his days he stays obligated to get up and take her back. Only there did the Torah reveal this. But here, what he did, he did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב פפא's question from step 16. A husband who divorced his wife for no reason does not have to take her back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gave a special rule for an אונס: if he divorces her, he must remarry her. רבא reasons that this rule had to be stated outright because it is unusual. So it applies only to the אונס. In any other case the divorce stands, even if it was done for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced a girl, whom the Torah commands to marry her
The Torah (literally, the Merciful One) revealed it
Get up and take her back
What he did, he did; the act stands

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying it is fine to divorce for no reason. He is only saying that once the divorce is done, the man is not forced to remarry her.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: From what the Merciful One revealed regarding a rapist:
"He may not send her away all his days"
all his days he stands under "get up and take her back";
it is there that the Merciful One revealed it,
but here, what he did, he did.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, מִדְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי אוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The divorce stands ('what he did, he did'), and he does not have to take her back. The duty to remarry applies only to an אונס, where the Torah states it outright.

steps.title: רב משרשיא asks about planning a divorce while living together
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא asks רבא about a man who has decided to divorce his wife while she still lives with him and takes care of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to רבא: If his heart is set on divorcing her, and she still lives with him and takes care of him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked. It is about a man who secretly plans to divorce his wife but keeps living with her as usual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer about the reason for divorce. It is about how the man acts in the meantime. Is it proper to keep enjoying her care while he has already decided to send her away?

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of רבא
His heart is set on divorcing her
She serves him; she lives with him as his wife

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said to Rava:
If his heart is set on divorcing her,
and she lives with him and serves him,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related question about divorce
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a man may keep living with his wife while he plans to divorce her

steps.title: רבא applies a verse: Do not plot against someone who trusts you
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with a פסוק from משלי that forbids plotting harm against someone who lives with you in trust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא read this פסוק about him: "Do not plan evil against your friend while he lives trustingly with you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב משרשיא with a פסוק. The man is doing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife trusts him and lives with him in peace. Meanwhile he is secretly planning to send her away. This is exactly what the פסוק forbids: plotting harm against someone who feels safe with you.

keyTerms.meaning: He read about him; he applied a פסוק to him

phrases.english: He read about him:
"Do not plot evil against your neighbor,
while he dwells securely with you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב משרשיא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is wrong, because of the פסוק "Do not plot evil against your neighbor".

steps.title: רבי מאיר: People treat wives like food; the overly strict man
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי מאיר compares men's attitudes to their wives with attitudes to food. The first type throws out the whole cup when a fly falls in. That is like פפוס בן יהודה, who locked his wife in.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say: Just as people have different attitudes toward food, so they have different attitudes toward women. Some people, when a fly falls into their cup, throw it out and do not drink it. That is the way of פפוס בן יהודה, who used to lock the door on his wife when he went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי מאיר describing different kinds of husbands. This step gives the first, overly strict kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fly stands for any small thing that might bother a husband about his wife. The first man is so fussy that he throws out the whole drink. In the same way, פפוס בן יהודה was so suspicious that he locked his wife in, so she would never see another man.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A man known for being very suspicious of his wife

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
Just as there are different attitudes about food,
so are there different attitudes about women.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁזְּבוּב נוֹפֵל לְתוֹךְ כּוֹסוֹ –
phrases.english: You have a person who, when a fly falls into his cup,
throws it out and does not drink it;

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ הִיא מִדַּת פַּפּוּס בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: and this is the way of Pappos ben Yehuda,
who would lock the door on his wife and go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא about husbands' attitudes, connected to the topic of divorce
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Husbands differ like eaters do; the first type is overly strict, like פפוס בן יהודה, who locked his wife in.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: The ordinary man
steps.stepSummary: The second type removes the fly and drinks the wine. That is the ordinary man, who lets his wife talk with her brothers and relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some people, when a fly falls into their cup, throw out the fly and drink. That is the way of most people: his wife talks with her brothers and relatives, and he lets her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר continues his ברייתא with the second, ordinary kind of husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man removes only the fly and still enjoys his drink. He does not throw out the whole thing over a small worry. In the same way, he does not mind when his wife speaks with her family, and he lets her do it.

keyTerms.meaning: He lets her; he leaves her be

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁזְּבוּב נוֹפֵל לְתוֹךְ כּוֹסוֹ –
phrases.english: And you have a person who, when a fly falls into his cup,
throws it out and drinks it;
phrases.notes: Here he throws out only the fly and drinks the rest.

phrases.english: and this is the way of every person,
whose wife speaks with her brothers and relatives,
and he lets her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁזְּבוּב נוֹפֵל לְתוֹךְ כּוֹסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי מאיר's ברייתא with the second type
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ordinary husband is not overly strict. He lets his wife speak with her relatives.

steps.title: The third type: the man who eats the food even with the fly
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר describes a third type of man. When a fly falls into his bowl, he sucks it and eats the food anyway. That is the bad man, who lets his wife go out with her head uncovered and spin thread in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a man who, when a fly falls into his bowl, sucks it and eats the food. This is the way of a bad man, who sees his wife going out with her head uncovered and spinning thread in the marketplace,
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third and last type in רבי מאיר's list. This is a man who does not care at all about his wife's immodest behavior. The description of what he allows is still going on, and the list continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first man threw out the whole cup, which is too much jealousy. The second man removed the fly and drank, which is normal and healthy. This third man does not even remove the fly; he sucks it and eats, so nothing bothers him. In the same way, he sees his wife acting immodestly in public and does nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: A serving bowl or dish of food
Her head uncovered (her hair not covered)
Spinning thread in the marketplace, out in public

steps.whyThisMatters: This third type completes the scale from too jealous, to balanced, to not caring at all. The ברייתא is building toward what should be done about such a marriage.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the change from cup to bowl. The first two types were about wine in a cup. This one is about food in a bowl. The point is the same: how much the man is bothered by the fly.

phrases.english: And there is a man
who, when a fly falls into his serving bowl
sucks it and eats it
this is the way of a bad man
who sees his wife going out
with her head uncovered
and spinning thread in the marketplace,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁזְּבוּב נוֹפֵל לְתוֹךְ תַּמְחוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third type to רבי מאיר's list, after the overly jealous man (step 20) and the ordinary man (step 21).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man who does not care at all, like one who sucks the fly and eats the food, is an אָדָם רַע. He sees his wife go out with her head uncovered and spin in the marketplace and does nothing.
